risks.name: Pay can be changed one-sided
risks.reason: Your pay can change without your agreement.
risks.question: Will any change to my pay need my written consent?
risks.safer_wording: Any change to compensation will be made only with the Employee's prior written consent.

risks.name: Terms can be changed one-sided
risks.reason: The other side can change the deal later without asking you.
risks.question: Will I be told in writing before any change, and can I exit without penalty if I disagree?
risks.safer_wording: Any change to these terms will be notified in writing at least 30 days in advance, and the other party may terminate without penalty if they do not accept it.

risks.name: Termination without notice
risks.reason: You can be let go or cut off immediately, with no time to prepare.
risks.question: What notice or compensation will I get if this is terminated, and for what reasons?
risks.safer_wording: Either party may terminate this agreement with 30 days' written notice, or immediately only for material breach after a written warning.

risks.name: Service bond / exit penalty
risks.reason: You may owe a large fixed penalty if you leave early. Indian courts usually allow only reasonable, proven compensation (Indian Contract Act, s.74), but you can still be pressured or sued.
risks.question: Is the bond amount reduced pro-rata for time served, and what exact costs does it cover?
risks.safer_wording: If the Employee leaves within 12 months, they will reimburse actual documented training costs, reduced pro-rata for each month served.

risks.name: Salary or documents can be withheld
risks.reason: Your final pay or certificates could be held back to stop you leaving.
risks.question: Under what exact conditions can my salary or documents be withheld, and for how long?
risks.safer_wording: Full and final settlement and relieving documents will be issued within 30 days of the last working day. Original certificates will be verified and returned the same day.

risks.name: Long notice period
risks.reason: A long notice period can make it hard to join a new job quickly.
risks.question: Is the notice period the same for both sides, and can I buy it out or have it waived?
risks.safer_wording: Either party may end employment with 30 days' written notice. The Employee may pay salary in lieu of any unserved notice.

risks.name: Non-compete after leaving
risks.reason: Limits where you can work next. Post-employment non-competes are generally void in India (Indian Contract Act, s.27), but can still be used to pressure you.
risks.question: Can this restriction be limited to not using confidential information, rather than not working in the field?
risks.safer_wording: After leaving, the Employee will not use or disclose the Company's confidential information. No other restriction on future employment applies.

risks.name: Probation can be extended at will
risks.reason: Your probation, with weaker job security, could be stretched out.
risks.question: What is the maximum probation length, and how will I be told if it is extended?
risks.safer_wording: Probation may be extended once, by up to 3 months, with written reasons given before the original period ends.

risks.name: Transfer to any location
risks.reason: You could be moved to another city without a say.
risks.question: Will any transfer need my consent, and will relocation costs be covered?
risks.safer_wording: Any transfer outside the current city will be made only with the Employee's consent, and reasonable relocation costs will be paid.

risks.name: Owns work done outside job
patterns: \b(whether or not|outside|beyond)\b[^.;]{0,20}\b(during )?(working hours|office hours|the scope of employment)\b
risks.reason: The other side may claim ownership of your personal projects too.
risks.question: Can ownership be limited to work done for this job, using company time or resources?
risks.safer_wording: The Company owns work created in the course of employment or using Company resources. Personal projects made outside working hours remain the Employee's.

risks.name: You give up the right to claim
risks.reason: You give up your right to claim damages even if they are at fault.
risks.question: Does this still let me claim if the other side is negligent or breaks the agreement?
risks.safer_wording: Nothing in this agreement limits either party's right to claim for the other's negligence, breach or fraud, or any statutory rights.

risks.name: Their liability is limited
risks.reason: If something goes wrong, the other side may pay little or nothing.
risks.question: Is there an exception for negligence, fraud or failure to deliver?
risks.safer_wording: Liability is limited to the amount paid, except for loss caused by negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or failure to deliver.

risks.name: No responsibility for delays
risks.reason: Deadlines may not be binding, with no remedy for late delivery.
risks.question: What happens, such as a discount or a right to cancel, if delivery is late?
risks.safer_wording: If delivery is more than 7 days late for reasons within the Provider's control, the Client may cancel with a full refund or receive a 5% discount per week of delay.

risks.name: Non-refundable payment
risks.reason: You may lose your money even if you cancel early or the service changes.
risks.question: Will I get a refund if the other side cancels or changes the service, or if I cancel early?
risks.safer_wording: A full refund will be given if the Provider cancels or materially changes the service, and a partial refund for cancellations made at least 7 days in advance.

risks.name: Extra or unclear fees
risks.reason: The final price may be higher than quoted, because extra fees or taxes are added later.
risks.question: What is the full final price including all taxes and fees?
risks.safer_wording: The quoted price is the total payable, inclusive of GST and all fees. Any other charge needs the Client's written approval in advance.

risks.name: Price can increase
risks.reason: The price you agreed may go up after you commit.
risks.question: Is this price fixed for the whole project or period?
risks.safer_wording: Prices are fixed for the duration of this engagement. Any increase needs the Client's written approval.

risks.name: Large advance payment
risks.reason: You pay most of the money before getting anything, which leaves you exposed.
risks.question: Can payment be split into milestones tied to delivery?
risks.safer_wording: 30% advance, 40% on delivery of the first draft and 30% on final acceptance.

risks.name: Heavy late-payment penalty
risks.reason: A small delay in paying could cost you a lot.
risks.question: Can the late-payment charge be reduced and given a grace period?
risks.safer_wording: Invoices are payable within 15 days. Late amounts carry simple interest of 12% per annum after a 7-day grace period.

risks.name: Automatic renewal
risks.reason: You may keep getting charged unless you remember to cancel.
risks.question: Will I get a reminder before renewal, and can I cancel any time?
risks.safer_wording: The subscription renews only after a reminder is sent at least 7 days in advance, and it can be cancelled at any time with no charge for the following period.

risks.name: They can cancel or change the event
patterns: \b(reserves? the right|may|can)\b[^.;]{0,15}\b(to )?(cancel|reschedule|postpone|change the venue|change the line-?up|substitute)\b
risks.reason: The event or service can be cancelled or changed, possibly without a refund.
risks.question: Do I get a full refund if the event is cancelled, postponed or materially changed?
risks.safer_wording: If the event is cancelled, postponed or materially changed, ticket holders may claim a full refund, including all fees, within 7 days.

risks.name: Cannot transfer
risks.reason: If you can't attend, you can't pass it on, so the money is lost.
risks.question: Can I transfer the ticket to someone else or get a credit if I can't attend?
risks.safer_wording: Tickets may be transferred once through the official platform at no extra charge.

risks.name: One-sided indemnity
risks.reason: You must cover their legal costs and losses, but they don't have to cover yours.
risks.question: Can the indemnity be made mutual and limited to losses I actually cause?
risks.safer_wording: Each party will indemnify the other only for losses directly caused by its own breach or negligence.

risks.name: Your data is shared
risks.reason: Your personal details may be passed to other companies.
risks.question: Which companies get my data, and can I opt out?
risks.safer_wording: Personal data will be shared with third parties only with the user's explicit opt-in consent, and the user may withdraw consent at any time.

risks.name: Disputes only in their city
risks.reason: You may have to fight a dispute in a far-away city. Consumers can usually still complain where they live under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
risks.question: Can disputes also be raised where I live?
risks.safer_wording: Disputes may be raised in the courts or consumer commissions where either party resides.

risks.name: Forced arbitration
risks.reason: You may lose access to normal courts. The arbitrator could be chosen by them, and costs can be high.
risks.question: Who picks the arbitrator, who pays, and can I still use consumer forums or courts?
risks.safer_wording: Disputes may be resolved by an arbitrator jointly appointed by both parties, with costs shared equally, without affecting either party's statutory remedies.

risks.name: Using it counts as agreeing
patterns: \bby (using|accessing|installing|downloading|registering|visiting|browsing|clicking|continuing to use|signing up|creating an account|purchasing|making a payment)\b[^.;]{0,100}\b(you )?(agree|accept|consent|acknowledge|indicate|confirm)\w*\b
risks.reason: Just using the service counts as agreeing, even if you never read or signed the terms, and that includes later changes.
risks.question: Where can I read every term I'm agreeing to by using this, and will I be told about changes?
risks.safer_wording: These terms apply only after the user actively accepts them, and any later change needs the user's fresh acceptance.

risks.name: Your content can be removed
patterns: \b(we|company|reserves? the right|has the right|right to|at (its|our) (sole )?(discretion|judgment)|(?<!you )may)\b[^.;]{0,50}\b(remove|delete|disable|block|reclaim|take down|refuse to (post|display|publish)|edit|withdraw|screen)\w*\b[^.;]{0,60}\b(content|account|username|posts?|photos?|virtual|materials?|data|communications?|listings?|items?|messages?)\b
risks.reason: Your posts, files, account data or purchased items can be deleted, possibly without warning or a refund.
risks.question: Will I be warned and allowed to download my content before anything is removed, and is there an appeal?
risks.safer_wording: Content will be removed only for a stated breach, after notice to the user, with a chance to appeal and to export their data first.

risks.name: A far-away law applies
patterns: \b(governed by|construed (and enforced )?in accordance with|interpreted in accordance with)\b[^.;]{0,60}\blaws?\b
risks.reason: The contract follows another country's or state's law, which may give you fewer protections than your local consumer law.
risks.question: Do my local consumer protection laws still apply to me?
risks.safer_wording: This agreement is governed by the laws of India, and nothing in it removes the consumer's statutory rights where they live.
